PART I

Item 1. Business

Example Test Systems, Inc. designs and sells wafer-level burn-in and test equipment to semiconductor manufacturers. The company was incorporated in California and reports in U.S. dollars. Our fiscal year ends on the last Friday in May.

Item 1A. Risk Factors

Our revenue depends on a small number of customers, and the loss of any one of them would reduce our net sales materially. A single customer accounted for 58% of revenue in fiscal 2026. Demand for wafer-level test equipment is cyclical, and a downturn in the semiconductor industry could cause orders to fall sharply. We compete with larger companies such as Rival Corp. that have greater financial resources. Our products contain complex components, and quality problems could delay shipments and damage our reputation. We rely on three suppliers for wafers, and a disruption at any of them could halt production for several months. Changes in U.S. trade policy, including tariffs on exports to Asia, could reduce demand or raise our costs. We have incurred net losses in prior years, and we may not sustain profitability. The market price of our common stock has been volatile and may decline regardless of our operating performance. Our growth strategy depends on winning a second hyperscale customer, and there is no assurance that we will.

Item 1B. Unresolved Staff Comments

None.

Item 2. Properties

Our headquarters and manufacturing facility are located in Fremont, California, under a lease expiring in 2029.

PART II

Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

Net sales for fiscal 2026 increased 46% to $84.2 million from $57.7 million in fiscal 2025, driven by shipments of wafer-level burn-in systems to our largest customer. Gross margin improved to 48.5% from 44.1% as volumes scaled and fixed costs were absorbed. Operating expenses rose 12% to $31.4 million, reflecting headcount growth in engineering. We recorded net income of $9.6 million compared with a net loss of $2.3 million in the prior year. Cash and investments totaled $62.0 million at year end, and we have no debt. Backlog at the end of the fiscal year was $28.0 million, up from $11.5 million. We expect fiscal 2027 revenue to grow significantly as AI processor customers move burn-in to the wafer. Bookings in the fourth quarter were the highest in the company's history. However, orders from our second-largest customer declined 35% as that customer worked through inventory. We expect gross margin to remain near 48% in fiscal 2027.

Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk

Our exposure to market risk is limited to interest income on cash equivalents.
